meta.label: Obesity / GLP-1 weight-management patient journey
notes: Chronological clinical arc, NOT an interview-guide recut. Fragments from any source can be tagged into these stages independent of how the source materials were structured.
The WCT GLP-1 corpus (wct_glp1_2025q4) is specifically about post-loss MAINTENANCE; expect fragments to concentrate in stages 4-7. Sparse coverage of stages 1-3 is expected, not a bug.
Stages 1-3 describe the pre-pharmacotherapy journey (lifestyle-only attempts → first clinical conversation → drug initiation). They exist so fragments narrating that history have somewhere to land.
Step granularity is intentionally moderate (2-3 steps per stage). Finer-grained sub-steps belong in journey-map artifact authoring, not in the registry.

stages.label: Lifestyle attempts
stages.description: Pre-pharmacotherapy period. Diet cycles, exercise programs, commercial weight-loss programs; building knowledge of what does and doesn't work for the individual; accumulating frustration with weight regain.

steps.label: Diet cycles
steps.description: Repeated weight-loss attempts via diet (keto, intermittent fasting, calorie counting, commercial programs); typically with eventual regain.

steps.label: Exercise attempts
steps.description: Structured or unstructured exercise as a weight-management strategy; often paired with diet.

steps.label: Plateau acceptance
steps.description: The point where the speaker has internalized that lifestyle alone has not produced durable results; readiness for medical intervention.

stages.label: First clinical conversation
stages.description: First substantive medical engagement about weight as a treatable condition. BMI / comorbidity evaluation, GLP-1 awareness, qualification discussion.

steps.label: PCP or specialist visit
steps.description: Initial appointment where weight is named as a clinical issue, not just a personal goal.

steps.label: Comorbidity / BMI evaluation
steps.description: Clinical assessment of weight-related risk (BMI, A1c, blood pressure, sleep apnea, etc.).

steps.label: GLP-1 qualification
steps.description: Discussion of GLP-1 / GIP eligibility, insurance coverage, and prescription decision.

stages.label: GLP-1 initiation
stages.description: Starting therapy. First doses, titration ladder, early side effects (nausea, fatigue), first changes in appetite/satiety.

steps.label: First doses
steps.description: Initial low-dose phase; learning injection technique; managing expectations.

steps.label: Titration
steps.description: Stepping up dose per the prescriber's schedule; common point of dropout if side effects are severe.

steps.label: Initial side effects
steps.description: GI side effects, fatigue, food aversions; deciding whether to push through.

stages.label: Active weight loss
stages.description: Visible weight loss while on therapy. Reshaping of eating habits; social and identity changes; engagement with weight-loss community.

steps.label: Visible progress
steps.description: Scale numbers move; clothes fit differently; external feedback from family / coworkers.

steps.label: Lifestyle integration
steps.description: Eating, exercise, and social patterns reshape around the medication's effects.

steps.label: Identity shift
steps.description: Self-concept changes ('I'm a person who has lost weight' / 'I'm a person on medication'); often ambivalent.

stages.label: Weight stabilization
stages.description: The 'maintenance' plateau. Target weight reached or approached; dose may be held; daily routine has stabilized around the medication.

steps.label: Target approached
steps.description: Weight near or at the personally-meaningful goal; loss rate slows.

steps.label: Dose continuation question
steps.description: Conversation with self / prescriber about whether to continue at full dose, taper, or hold.

steps.label: Daily normalization
steps.description: Medication becomes a routine fixture rather than a project.

stages.label: Discontinuation consideration
stages.description: Active weighing of staying on vs. coming off. Cost, side-effect fatigue, supply issues, clinical guidance, and personal philosophy all in play.

steps.label: Cost pressure
steps.description: Out-of-pocket cost, insurance changes, supply / compounding considerations driving the question.

steps.label: Side-effect fatigue
steps.description: Cumulative tolerance burden — even mild side effects sustained over time become a reason to stop.

steps.label: Clinical taper discussion
steps.description: Prescriber-led conversation about safe discontinuation, taper schedules, and what to expect.

stages.label: Post-discontinuation
stages.description: Off therapy. Short-term stability vs. emerging regain; attempted self-maintenance; awareness of the body's drive to return to higher weight.

steps.label: Short-term stability
steps.description: The first weeks/months off, when weight typically holds and the speaker is most optimistic.

steps.label: Regain awareness
steps.description: First noticing weight creeping back; appetite return; reassessment of the discontinuation decision.

steps.label: Attempted self-maintenance
steps.description: Doubling down on lifestyle to hold the loss without medication.

stages.label: Clinical-trial consideration
stages.description: Hearing about and weighing a clinical trial — in the WCT GLP-1 case, a maintenance trial for people who have discontinued and are at risk of regain. This stage is where the WCT corpus is densest.

steps.label: Trial awareness
steps.description: Hearing about the trial; first impressions of what it is and what it would involve.

steps.label: Eligibility self-assessment
steps.description: Working out whether the trial's criteria (weight loss history, discontinuation window, stability period) apply to oneself.

steps.label: Logistics assessment
steps.description: Travel, time commitment, financial implications, work / family compatibility.

steps.label: Consent or decline
steps.description: The decision moment — would I do it, on what terms, and why or why not.
